rationale: Selected boundary: execution_plan scope, group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, whose only call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (target project.invoke, phase run) is the complete accumulated training step; this candidate explicitly replaces the installed bundle trial-ee9a17b054-param-286bf06b on that same call and preserves its behavior itself (the gloo control-group barrier after the final microbatch forward, immediately before its backward). How previous feedback changes this attempt: trial-ee9a17b054 was accepted and measured (paired AB/BA) at objective 36.281 ms vs parent 44.515 ms with step_ms 110.7/112.0 under the 121.51 ms limit, so the barrier is now preserved baseline behavior, not a new claim; its manifest code (inspected byte-for-byte) confirms the barrier is the only insertion and that gradients are bit-identical, which this candidate keeps verbatim. The remaining objective is transport-bound, not skew-bound: the non-waiting rank pays 32.65-32.79 ms of pure kernel time (12x1.855-1.892 ms at 28,351,488 B + 10.17-10.32 ms at 157,541,376 B, ~15.0-15.3 GB/s per collective), the residual max-rank excess is only 2.3-4.9 ms of in-kernel waiting (inside the last evaluation's MAD noise bounds 0.44/4.10 ms), NCCL 2.29.7 runs RING over SHM with only 2 channels (nccl_tuning evidence: AllReduce 28,351,488 B and 157,541,376 B both RING/SIMPLE channel{0..1}; the in-model kernels run RING_LL at 15.2 vs 14.3 GB/s for the same sizes under default SIMPLE), P2P peer access is unavailable and telemetry sustains pcie.rx 14.5-14.7 GB/s against a PCIe gen4 x16 link - so the floor is channel/protocol limited with headroom, exactly as the collection plan left open. Because the default PG's NCCL communicator is created in prepare() before build(), the only host-reachable way to change channels/protocol for the 13 bucket allreduces is a NEW communicator created by the candidate and a DDP comm hook routing the buckets onto it; wiring the hook is only coherent jointly with re-issuing the whole step, so the replacement reproduces adapter.run verbatim (identical zero_grad(set_to_none=True), no_sync schedule, forward labels=tokens/use_cache=False, loss/total backward, loss bookkeeping, discovery phase contexts, optimizer.step()+cuda.synchronize, identical result structure) plus the preserved barrier. The hook is torch 2.13's default_hooks.allreduce_hook (div by group size then SUM allreduce), documented as behavior-preserving versus the default reducer and the same hook the source's own bucket-inventory diagnostic uses; bucket count (13), payloads, DDP bucket timing and backward overlap are unchanged, gradients stay bitwise identical across ranks (NCCL yields identical per-collective results on every rank, so the atol=0/rtol=0 exact_gradient_replica_check is intact) and the div-then-SUM rounding difference versus the default reducer stays far inside the 1e-6/1e-4 grad/parameter tolerances against the serial global-batch reference. Hypothesis to be falsified by the paired protocol: creating the new group in build() under NCCL_MAX_CHANNELS raised to 8-16 (parameter-tunable, default 8) with NCCL_PROTO constrained to the measured LL family (default LL) lifts per-collective effective bandwidth above the 15.0-15.3 GB/s floor, shrinking every ncclDevKernel_AllReduce kernel duration; with 497.8 MB total payload each +1 GB/s is worth ~2.1 ms off the objective, while the preserved barrier should hold residual wait at or below the current 2.3-4.9 ms. Concrete regression path checked before any benefit is claimed: if the new communicator silently selects SIMPLE the synthetic floor is 34.3 ms (12x1.977+10.587) > the current 32.7 ms kernel floor, which must be visible in the profiled kernel names (LL vs SIMPLE variants) and would fail the paired gain requirement; nccl_max_channels=2 and nccl_proto=auto remain in the parameter space as measured controls, and if channel count does not lift SHM bandwidth the paired gains must fall inside the noise bounds and the candidate must not be accepted.

setup_work.performed_in: build(context) on every rank before any invocation; setup receipt timing captures it and the measured warm-model region excludes it
steps: Save current NCCL_MAX_CHANNELS and NCCL_PROTO environment values.
Set NCCL_MAX_CHANNELS (parameter, default 8) and, unless the parameter is 'auto', NCCL_PROTO (default 'LL') for this worker process only.

Create a new nccl process group via dist.new_group(backend='nccl', timeout=300s, device_id=<rank device>) - a collective, symmetric call executed by both ranks in build - with eager device_id initialization.

Warm the new group with one 4-byte allreduce of a zeros(1) CUDA tensor plus torch.cuda.synchronize() so the communicator and its channels are materialized under the raised environment, and verify the result is finite.
Restore the saved environment exactly; the default process group's communicator (created in prepare()) is untouched.
Register the comm hook: model.register_comm_hook(new_group, torch.distributed.algorithms.ddp_comm_hooks.default_hooks.allreduce_hook) on the DDP module from state, before any backward has run.
setup_work.memory: One fp32 scalar CUDA tensor (4 bytes, freed) plus the new NCCL communicator's internal allocations, which scale with channel count (per-channel buffers) and are driver-side, outside the PyTorch allocator counters (framework.peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle peaks do not see them; do not read a counter decrease as a physical-memory saving). No model parameter is transformed, packed or copied; retained PyTorch allocations are unchanged by setup.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: The comm hook stays installed on the DDP module for the worker's lifetime and is behavior-preserving (documented div-then-SUM average), so every subsequent invocation - warmup, repeats, profiled diagnostics and quality checks - uses the same reduction semantics; reset()/load_state_dict and the initial-state snapshot in prepare() are unaffected because the hook only changes which communicator performs the bucket allreduces. Parent endpoints of the paired protocol run in fresh workers, so no cross-contamination of measurements is possible. The new process group performs no collective outside the DDP bucket reductions after its one build-time warmup allreduce; all collective participation (control-group barriers, observe() broadcasts on the default group) is preserved on every rank.
setup_work.fallbacks: Structural setup failure (state shape) yields a labelled parent passthrough 'fallback:setup_guard_parent_step'; new-group creation or hook registration failure yields 'fallback:pg_setup_failed_parent_step' - both keep the parent (barrier bundle) behavior and leave the objective unchanged rather than incorrect. The preserved barrier degrades to a no-op only if the control group is absent (not the case in prepare()).

quality_risks: Protocol regression risk: if the new communicator selects SIMPLE instead of the LL family, the measured synthetic floor is 34.3 ms > the current 32.7 ms kernel floor, a possible objective regression; mitigated by defaulting nccl_proto to LL, by checking the profiled ncclDevKernel_AllReduce kernel names for the protocol actually chosen, and by the paired AB/BA acceptance rule (gains must exceed MAD-derived noise bounds 0.44/4.10 ms).

step_ms risk: the per-bucket hook adds one c10d allreduce dispatch versus the reducer's built-in launch, and the new communicator's first-use cost is absorbed at build/warmup outside the timed region; step_ms headroom is ~9.5 ms against the 121.51 ms limit and the preserved barrier keeps the accepted wait pattern, but a slower communicator would raise step_ms alongside the objective and be rejected by the same paired protocol.

Numerics: default_hooks.allreduce_hook divides by group size before the SUM, while the default reducer averages after reduction; for fp32 gradients this is a rounding-level difference (~1e-7 relative), far inside grad_atol=1e-6/grad_rtol=1e-4 and parameter_atol=1e-6/parameter_rtol=1e-4 versus the serial global-batch reference. Cross-rank bitwise equality (exact_gradient_replica_check atol=0/rtol=0) holds because NCCL allreduce returns identical bits on every rank, as in the accepted parent.

Collective symmetry: dist.new_group and the build-time warmup allreduce are executed identically on both ranks inside build(); guards depend only on shared context (world_size, dist state, state shape), so ranks cannot diverge into a half-created group. If creation raised on one rank only, the store rendezvous would surface as a setup failure/timeout rather than wrong results.

Metric semantics: the 13 gradient allreduces still execute as 13 NCCL kernels on the new communicator - communication_kernel_sum_ms still sums device kernel durations including waiting, so any gain must come from shorter kernel durations (higher effective bandwidth), not from fewer or hidden collectives; no measurement boundary or threshold is changed.

Persistent side effect: the comm hook remains on the DDP module after a hypothetical rollback because it is module state, not a returned callable; it is documented behavior-preserving, and the framework's fresh-worker parent endpoints are unaffected.

Unknown effects: whether more SHM channels raise effective bandwidth on this host (topology NODE, no P2P) is the hypothesis under test - channel counts 2/4/8/16 and protocol choices auto/LL/LL128/'LL,LL128' are declared for the existing TaskSearch/TPE loop, whose screening endpoints are finite differences, not acceptance evidence; acceptance still requires the paired project measurements.

params.name: nccl_max_channels
params.description: NCCL_MAX_CHANNELS applied only while the candidate's new nccl process group is created in build(); 2 reproduces the measured 2-channel default as a control, 8 is the default, 16 tests the upper headroom. Restored after creation; the default process group's communicator is unaffected.

params.name: nccl_proto
params.description: NCCL_PROTO constraint for the new communicator ('auto' leaves the environment untouched and lets NCCL tune, which measured RING/SIMPLE at 2 channels in the calibration worker; 'LL' preserves the in-model kernels' measured 15.2 GB/s advantage and is the default).
